expected.finding: **[P2]** **The write guards allow policy and history destinations to be swapped.** In [revise-improvement-policy.py:921](/home/runner/work/open-inspect-72e95a/open-inspect-72e95a/scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py:921), both paths use the same allowlist; checking that they differ does not enforce their roles. With a valid single-line policy, swapped arguments exit successfully while corrupting the policy with appended JSON and replacing the history with a policy document. Validate each destination against its specific role before writing.

**[P2]** **The dashboard’s reproduction command fails.** [render-rsi-dashboard.py:509](/home/runner/work/open-inspect-72e95a/open-inspect-72e95a/scripts/render-rsi-dashboard.py:509) invokes `measure-policy-validity.py` with unsupported `--repo-dir` and `--save-evidence` arguments. It exits with code 2, preventing the documented refresh. Use `mine-trace-failures.py` to collect evidence, then measure with `--trace-evidence` and `--out-json`.

+):
+    # v2 had a "pytest-runs" topic that classified the pytest failure; v3
+    # rolled it back. The failure is fresh field evidence for the retired
+    # definition (so re-mining it is judged on real counts) AND a blind spot
+    # of the current policy (so it can be mined again) (Codex, round 34).
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mine, "run_traces_json", _fake_runner({"t1": _events()}))
+    current = policy_mod.builtin_policy()

+    history = tmp_path / "h.jsonl"
+    history.write_text(
+        json.dumps({"version": 2, "policy": v2})
+        + "\n"
+        + json.dumps({"version": 3, "origin": "rollback", "policy": current})
+        + "\n"
+    )
+    out = tmp_path / "failures.json"
+    evidence = tmp_path / "evidence.json"
+    code = mine.main(
+        [
+            "m",
+            "--repo-dir",
+            "/repo",
+            "--policy",

+            "--history",
+            str(history),
+            "--out-json",
+            str(out),
+            "--save-evidence",
+            str(evidence),
+        ]
+    )
+    assert code == 0

+    report = json.loads(out.read_text())
+    assert "pytest-runs" not in report["by_topic"]
+    assert any("failed" in b["excerpt"] for b in report["blind_spots"])
